page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on x86_64 architecture using KVM virtualization. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz, it supplies 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The server includes 32 GB of memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, alongside 35 MB of L3 cache, 1 MB L2 cache per core, and hardware instruction flags including AVX-512 and AES. The instance features no integrated local storage or discrete GPUs, relying on 5 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth for communication.

Benchmark evaluations highlight a strong emphasis on multi-threaded parallel throughput over single-core speed. Single-core performance falls in the lower 25% of benchmarked systems, demonstrated by a stress-ng single-core score of 1107.09 and Geekbench single-core score of 1025.0. Conversely, multi-threaded evaluations perform within average ranges, achieving a multi-core stress-ng score of 11807.11 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 6333.0. Uncached memory read bandwidth averages 61.39 GB/sec, while write operations reach 55.37 GB/sec.

Qualitative cost efficiency is centered on multi-threaded workload scaling rather than single-threaded acceleration. With zero bundled local storage, persistent disk performance depends entirely on remote network storage. The instance achieves average performance in software compilation using Clang (10468.0), Redis SET operations (11.41 million ops/sec), and static web serving (9.93 GB/sec). These characteristics position the server effectively for CI/CD build runners, middle-tier web servers, Redis caching layers, and distributed batch processing jobs.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.4xlarge is a dedicated x86_64 compute-optimized instance utilizing KVM virtualization. Equipped with an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz, it offers 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores, 32 GB of RAM, and 35 MB of L3 cache. It features AVX-512 vector extensions and 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without bundled local storage or GPUs. Performance testing reveals a distinct contrast: single-threaded scores, including single-core stress-ng and gzip compression, rank in the lower quartile, whereas multi-core benchmarks show average efficiency, marked by a multi-core stress-ng score of 11807.11 and software compilation scores of 10468.0. Uncached memory read bandwidth averages 61.39 GB/sec. This hardware profile provides reliable qualitative cost efficiency for horizontally scalable, multi-threaded workloads such as CI/CD build clusters, static web serving, Redis caches, and moderate database services.
